prompt: What does `inject(Greeter)` in a component's field do?

choices.text: It creates a fresh `Greeter` with `new`, every time the field is read
choices.why: The field is set once, and the instance comes from an injector, not from `new` in the component.

choices.text: It asks an injector for one and keeps the answer
choices.why: Right. The component never builds it.

choices.text: It imports the file where `Greeter` is written
choices.why: The `import` line does that; `inject` asks for an instance at run time.

choices.text: It registers `Greeter` so other components can use it
choices.why: Registering is what a provider does; `inject` only asks.

prompt: `Greeter` was marked `@Injectable()` with nothing inside the brackets, and the bench asked for one. What happened?

choices.text: The bench showed an empty paragraph
choices.why: Nothing of the application past the heading appeared.

choices.text: The build failed before the page loaded
choices.why: The build passed; the error came when the page ran.

choices.text: `NG0201`: no injector had a recipe, and the app stopped at the heading
choices.why: Right. `@Injectable()` alone says Angular may build it, not where.

choices.text: Angular built one anyway, since the class was marked
choices.why: The mark is not a recipe; no injector was told about it.

prompt: `@Injectable({ providedIn: '___' })` makes one instance for the whole application, the first time it is asked for.
Older code writes `constructor(private readonly greeter: Greeter) {}`. Compared with `inject(Greeter)` in a field, what is different?

choices.text: The parameter gets a new `Greeter` per component; `inject` shares one
choices.why: Both ask the same injector and get the same answer.

choices.text: Nothing about the answer; `inject` also works outside a constructor's parameters
choices.why: Right. Same question, same injector.

choices.text: The parameter form is no longer allowed in Angular 21
choices.why: It still works and you will read plenty of it.

choices.text: The parameter form skips the injector and calls `new`
choices.why: Angular reads the type and asks the injector.

prompt: Match each provider key with what the injector answers.

pairs.right: an instance of that class, made once

right_distractors: a fresh instance on every request

prompt: `Greeter` had `providedIn: 'root'`, and `app.config.ts` listed `{ provide: Greeter, useClass: LoudGreeter }`. What did the bench show?

choices.text: `Hello, Ana`, because the class's own recipe comes first
choices.why: The listed provider wins; the class's own is the default.

choices.text: `HELLO, ANA!`
choices.why: Right. The bench asked for `Greeter` and was answered with a `LoudGreeter`.

choices.text: An error, since two recipes for one token clash
choices.why: A list entry overriding a default is the normal case.

choices.text: Both greetings, one after the other
choices.why: One token, one answer.

prompt: What does `provideRouter(routes)` in `app.config.ts` put in the list?

choices.text: The routes array, used as a token
choices.why: The routes are an argument; what comes back is providers.

choices.text: One component that draws the router
choices.why: A provider list holds recipes, not components to draw.

choices.text: Several providers for the router's classes
choices.why: Right. A `provide...` function gathers them behind one name.

choices.text: A setting that turns on the `<router-outlet>` tag
choices.why: The tag comes from `RouterOutlet` in a component's `imports`.

prompt: The provider list `providers: [Greeter]` is the short form of `{ provide: Greeter, ___: Greeter }`.
Why does the planner need `InjectionToken` for today, rather than `inject(Date)`?

choices.text: `inject(Date)` asks for the class, not a day
choices.why: Right. A token stands for a value that is not a class.

choices.text: `Date` cannot be imported into an Angular component
choices.why: It is a global of the language; nothing stops you using it.

choices.text: An `InjectionToken` reads the clock more precisely
choices.why: It reads nothing; its factory calls `new Date()`, the same clock.

choices.text: Tokens are the only things a test may override
choices.why: A test can override a class token just as well.

prompt: The planner stays open from Sunday evening to Monday morning. Which week does it count on Monday?

choices.text: The new week, because `TODAY` reads the clock whenever it is injected
choices.why: The factory runs once, the first time, and its answer is kept.

choices.text: The old one, until the page is loaded again
choices.why: Right. `TODAY` is the moment it was first asked for.

choices.text: Neither: `Week` throws when the date moves
choices.why: Nothing watches the date, so nothing throws.

choices.text: The new one, because `--today` moves the clock
choices.why: `--today` exists only in `look`, for the transcripts.

prompt: The first `week.spec.ts` expected the week of 26 October and failed. Why did the second one pass, on the same day?

choices.text: It waited for the data before reading the page
choices.why: Neither version loaded the data; the range does not need it.

choices.text: It moved the computer's clock forward by five days first
choices.why: Nothing touched the clock.

choices.text: `TestBed` reads dates from `courses.json`
choices.why: The test never reached `courses.json`.

choices.text: It gave `TODAY` a `useValue` in the test's providers
choices.why: Right. The test's recipe wins over the token's factory.

prompt: With `TODAY` set to Wednesday, 28 October 2026, on which day of October does the week the planner counts begin?
`Tally` had `providedIn: 'root'` and no component listed it. One click on `Add to first`: what did the two counters show?

choices.text: first: 1, second: 0
choices.why: That is the version where each counter lists `Tally` in its own `providers`.

choices.text: first: 1, second: 1
choices.why: Right. Both questions reached the root, which made one `Tally`.

choices.text: first: 2, second: 0
choices.why: One click adds one, to one shared tally.

choices.text: An `NG0201`, since no component provided it
choices.why: The root had the recipe from `providedIn`.

prompt: Put the injectors in the order `inject(Tally)` in a `Counter` asks them, first to last.
A service is listed in a component's `providers`. How long does the instance it makes live?

choices.text: As long as the application, like any service
choices.why: That is a root provider; a component's list makes one per component.

choices.text: Until the next change detection
choices.why: Change detection does not make or destroy instances.

choices.text: As long as that component
choices.why: Right. It is made with it and goes when it is destroyed.

choices.text: Until somebody else asks for one at the root
choices.why: The root's recipe is separate and does not replace it.

prompt: Why will one root instance fix the disagreement between `Week` and `CoursePage`?

choices.text: Root services load data faster
choices.why: Speed is not the problem; two copies are.

choices.text: It turns off the second fetch of `courses.json` in the dev server
choices.why: The dev server answers whatever is asked; the change is in who asks.

choices.text: Both screens get the same instance, so there is one copy of the data
choices.why: Right. A toggle on one is then seen by the other.

choices.text: `providedIn: 'root'` makes the data read-only
choices.why: It decides who shares the instance, not whether it changes.

prompt: Match each option of `inject` with what it changes.

pairs.right: only the component's own injector is asked
the question starts at the parent
the question stops at the host component

right_distractors: the instance is made again for every read

prompt: After one click on `Add to first` and one on `Add to second`, each counter showed `1, all: 2`. Where did `all` come from?

choices.text: From the bench, which added up the two counters' numbers
choices.why: The bench holds no tally of its own.

choices.text: From the root's `Tally`, reached with `skipSelf`
choices.why: Right. Skipping its own injector, each counter found the shared one.

choices.text: From `NOTE`, which nobody provided
choices.why: `NOTE` was `null`, and the page showed `no note`.

choices.text: From a second `providers: [Tally]` on the bench
choices.why: The bench has no `providers` list in this version.

prompt: An `NG0201` appears for a service that should always exist. Why does the lesson advise against `optional: true` there?

choices.text: It is slower than a normal injection
choices.why: Speed is not the argument.

choices.text: It only works on tokens, not on classes
choices.why: It works on both.

choices.text: It swaps a clear error now for a `null` found later
choices.why: Right. The missing provider is the bug to fix.

choices.text: It makes the component skip its own injector
choices.why: That is `skipSelf`.

prompt: `report()` called `inject(Tally)` when the button was clicked. What happened?

choices.text: `NG0203`: by then nothing was being built, so there was no injector to ask
choices.why: Right. A method runs long after construction.

choices.text: `NG0201`: nobody provided `Tally`
choices.why: `Tally` had `providedIn: 'root'`; the timing was the problem.

choices.text: The count was logged as 0, as in the fixed version
choices.why: The log only appeared once `inject` moved into a field.

choices.text: The build refused the file
choices.why: It compiled; the error came at the click.

prompt: Where may `inject()` be called? Choose every place that works.

choices.text: In a field's initialiser
choices.why: Right. Fields are set while the class is built.

choices.text: In the constructor
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: In a plain function called from a field
choices.why: Right. What matters is when it runs.

choices.text: In a click handler
choices.why: That runs after construction: `NG0203`.

choices.text: In a `setTimeout` started by the constructor
choices.why: The callback runs later, outside the context.

prompt: A component reads `localStorage` directly to find the user's theme, and its test cannot set one. What does this lesson suggest?

choices.text: Clear `localStorage` before every test, so each starts from nothing
choices.why: That gives every test the same theme, not the one it wants.

choices.text: A token with a factory reading it, overridden in the test
choices.why: Right. The component asks; the test decides the answer.

choices.text: Mark the component `@Injectable()`
choices.why: Components are already built by injectors; the problem is what it reads.

choices.text: Move the read into `ngOnInit`
choices.why: Later is still the same global, still not settable.
